contract_changes.before: For a face \(\sigma_0\) of \(K\), let \(C_{\sigma_0}\) be the subcomplex of faces \(\eta\) such that \(\eta\cup\sigma_0\) is a face. It contracts to the barycenter of \(\sigma_0\): for any point in a simplex \(\eta\) of \(C_{\sigma_0}\), the straight segment to that barycenter lies in the simplex \(\eta\cup\sigma_0\). On a chain simplex with smallest face \(\sigma_0\), the subdivision homeomorphism \(h\) lands in \(C_{\sigma_0}\); step 3.1 puts \(g\) in \(U_{\sigma_0}\), so every active vertex of \(f g\) forms a face jointly with \(\sigma_0\), and \(f g\) also lands in \(C_{\sigma_0}\). A face of the chain simplex has either the same smallest face or a larger one, whose carrier is contained in \(C_{\sigma_0}\). Induct over the finite simplices of \(\operatorname{sd}K\): the two endpoint maps and the already constructed boundary homotopy define a map from the boundary of each prism into its contractible carrier \(C_{\sigma_0}\); coning that boundary map to the carrier's barycenter extends the homotopy over the prism, relative to its boundary. The finite extensions paste continuously and give \(f g\simeq h\). Thus \(g h^{-1}\) is a homotopy inverse for \(f\), by steps 4.1 and 5.1. [F1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, induction, construct] ∎
